canonical_definition: Visual Reasoning is the ability to analyze and reason over visual inputs (e.g., images, videos, screenshots) to derive conclusions, select actions, or solve complex tasks, often involving pattern recognition, spatial reasoning, or interpretation of visualized interactions. Some definitions extend this to include multimodal reasoning with text or localization of relevant visual regions, while others emphasize its role in planning, program synthesis, or problem-solving with visual sketches. Disagreements exist in scope, with some framing it as a set of domain-general cognitive abilities and others focusing on task-specific applications in embodied or interactive environments.
